locator: PDF p. 20 (article p.17), Supervenience of Grounding
interpretation: His facts do not include grounding-relation instances as further facts. Equality only of bearer-existence facts is not the complete supervenience base.
attribution: The passage states if two worlds agree on which facts obtain, they agree on which facts ground which; this proposed supervenience principle uses all facts, not just a selected pair of relata, which is the premise.
